findings.text: Exported predicate tests whether a program counter value lies inside the cpuidle text region delimited by its start and end markers.
Helper structure pairs a high resolution timer with an integer completion flag used to signal expiry to a waiting idle loop.
Timer callback marks its container completion flag as set, requests rescheduling of the current task, and indicates no restart.

Forced idle entry validates FIFO policy with single CPU affinity, kernel thread context without memory management and without affinity changes, and non-zero duration, then disables preemption, marks idle, selects deep idle state from latency, arms a pinned hard monotonic timer for the duration, repeatedly idles until completion, and finally restores state and re-enables preemption with folded reschedule.
Boot entry marks the current task idle, prepares architecture idle, signals online idle state, then loops in the idle handler forever.
Idle class task placement always retains the current CPU assignment and never migrates idle tasks.
Idle class load balancing is unexpected and triggers a one-time warning diagnostic.
Idle class wakeup preemption unconditionally requests rescheduling on the runqueue.
Leaving the idle task refreshes its execution accounting, notifies the extension layer of idle exit, and updates the runqueue average idle metric.
Idle execution accounting measures elapsed task clock since last start, ignores non-positive deltas, advances the start timestamp, and forwards the delta to fair and extension deadline servers.
Entering the idle task updates core idle tracking, notifies the extension layer of idle entry, increments the go-idle counter, records execution start from task clock, and refreshes idle PELT clock.

Idle PELT handling sums fair, real-time and deadline utilization and, when the total reaches a computed capacity threshold, accumulates the gap between task clock and PELT clock as lost idle time before refreshing the idle PELT clock.
Core idle update is performed only when symmetric multithreading scheduling is active.
Removing an idle task from its runqueue is treated as erroneous, emitting a diagnostic and stack trace while temporarily releasing and reacquiring the runqueue lock.
Idle class tick only refreshes current idle execution accounting and takes no other action.
Switching to idle through the generic switch path is fatal, and changing idle priority is fatal unless old and new priorities are equal.
Housekeeping flag values correspond to single-bit positions derived from domain boot, domain, managed IRQ and kernel noise type identifiers.
Housekeeping state holds an array of RCU protected CPU mask pointers indexed by type plus a flags word, with one static instance.
A static branch key records whether any housekeeping isolation has been configured.
Helper constrains a task CPU affinity to the mask for a given type only when isolation is enabled and that type flag is set.
Membership test returns true when isolation is disabled or the type is not isolated, otherwise tests the CPU against the type mask.

Runtime update builds a trial domain mask excluding isolated CPUs, rejects empty intersection with online CPUs, enables the override key on first use, publishes the new mask with RCU protection, waits for readers, flushes PCI, memory cgroup and VM statistics work, then updates unbound workqueues, timer migration exclusion, and kernel threads before freeing the old mask.

Early initialization returns when no flags are set, otherwise enables the override key, initializes tick offload when kernel noise isolation is requested, and reallocates each boot-time mask to heap memory while queuing the old block for later release.
Tick offload initialization in this configuration is a no-operation reporting success.
Late initialization drains the list of boot-time mask blocks and releases each with the memblock allocator.

Boot parameter setup parses a CPU list into a non-housekeeping set, derives the housekeeping complement from possible CPUs, ensures at least one present CPU remains for housekeeping with fallback to the boot CPU, rejects empty isolation, handles first versus second configuration calls with equality checks between calls and a requirement for a shared present CPU outside noise and domain sets when both are involved, installs per-type masks from staging, triggers full tick setup for kernel noise on first use, and records the flags.

Isolcpus parameter parsing recognizes nohz, domain with boot domain, and managed IRQ prefixes, skips unknown alphabetic flags with an informational message, rejects flags containing illegal characters, and defaults to domain isolation when no flag is given.
Load average subsystem maintains an atomic count of active tasks, a timestamp for the next update window, and three exponentially decayed average values.
Accessor returns the three load averages each adjusted by a caller offset and left shifted by a caller shift.
Fixed-point helper raises a fractional base to an integer power using binary exponentiation with rounding after each multiply and shift.
Multi-interval decay helper applies the fixed-point power of the decay factor over a given count to update a load value with the current active count.
No-hertz accounting uses two atomic delta slots plus an integer index whose parity selects the active slot.
Read index helper masks the global index to select the stable slot for draining.
Entering no-hertz mode folds any pending per-runqueue delta into the shared no-hertz accumulation.

Exiting no-hertz mode synchronizes the per-runqueue update timestamp from the global window, returns early when still before the window, otherwise advances the timestamp when waking inside the following window to skip duplicate accounting; the companion read helper atomically drains the stable delta slot when non-zero.

Global no-hertz catch-up computes how many update intervals were missed, folds the active task count into the three averages over that count, advances the global timestamp accordingly, orders the timestamp write before the index increment, then flips the double-buffer index.
When no-hertz load accounting is disabled, the drain helper always yields zero and the global catch-up helper performs no action.

Periodic global update returns when still inside the sample window, otherwise folds the drained no-hertz delta into the active count, refreshes the three averages from the scaled active value, advances the window by one interval, and invokes catch-up for missed intervals.
Command mask aggregates global, global expedited with registration, private expedited with registration, sync-core and restartable-sequence variants when enabled else zero, plus get-registrations.
Expedited coordination uses one global IPI mutex plus one per-CPU mutex, with guard helpers for global and per-CPU serialization, initialized for every possible CPU at boot.

Remote handlers provide a plain memory barrier, a barrier plus deferred core synchronization, a barrier plus restartable-sequence state refresh with separate paths for legacy and version two modes, and a runqueue state synchronization that only acts when the current memory context matches the target and orders the update with a barrier.
Exec handling orders prior accesses before clearing the memory context barrier state and synchronizes the local runqueue copy.
Context switch helper loads barrier state from the next memory context when present and updates the runqueue copy only on change.

Global expedited path returns immediately on a single online CPU, otherwise allocates a temporary mask, serializes with memory barrier, IPI mutex and CPU read lock, collects online CPUs other than the caller that have the global expedited runqueue flag and a user context, then issues synchronous IPIs to that set with preemption disabled.
Visible prefix of the private expedited path obtains the current memory context and selects a default IPI handler before testing sync-core flags; the remainder is not in the fragment.
Housekeeping masks are published with RCU assignment and read under RCU protection, with a grace period wait after replacement and reallocation that preserves free-with-generic-allocator semantics.
Idle dequeue diagnostic path releases the runqueue interrupt-safe spinlock around reporting and reacquires it before returning.
